title: Priority vs partition co-tenancy sweep for stella
description: Compare (a) one model with priority_levels + PRIORITY header against (b) two model configs over the same weights with split instance_group counts. Ramp indexing offered load while search holds 100 TPS; find the indexing load at which search p99 crosses 100ms.

title: Open-loop two-class load generator with Triton priority header
description: Closed-loop loadgen cannot answer a co-tenancy question: with fixed worker counts, indexing steals capacity by construction. Need fixed OFFERED rate per class, priority header, per-second TPS + latency per class, and client-side back-pressure detection (due->send wait) so a client ceiling cannot masquerade as a server limit.

title: Partition instances instead of prioritising: dedicated search instance group
description: The co-tenancy sweep showed priority does not move the capacity cliff (~100-110 total rps on the 3080 at ic4) -- it only changes the shape of the failure past it. If production really needs 100 TPS of search AT a latency SLO, priority is the wrong tool. Test partitioning instead: give search its own model instance(s) so the two classes stop sharing a queue and a batch. Options to compare: (a) two model repos in one server, stella-search and stella-index, with instance_group counts summing to <=4, which gives each class its own instances and its own queue; (b) one repo with count=4 but a max_queue_delay tuned so search batches stay short; (c) two containers sharing the GPU. Measure search p99 at 100 TPS while indexing is over-offered, and find the search-instance count where p99 fits the SLO. Note VRAM: each instance is ~1.2 GB, so 4 instances total is the practical ceiling at 10 GB.

title: Rewrite load generator so it can offer its target rate
description: Both loadgen.py and priorityload.py are CPython threads doing blocking urllib calls. In the co-tenancy sweep the client could not offer 120 rps of 512-token documents at the loudest step (31.9 delivered against 120 offered, cap_wait_max 11s), so indexing capacity is only bounded to somewhere between 30 and 80 rps once search takes 100 TPS. Rewrite with multiprocessing or asyncio+httpx (or use a real load tool), verify it can offer 200+ rps of long payloads against an idle-enough server, then re-run priority-sweep.sh to pin down the indexing headroom. Also worth adding: report client-side offered-rate shortfall explicitly in the summary so a client ceiling can never again be read as a server capacity number.

title: Line graph of per-class TPS under indexing ramp
description: Read merged JSONL from the priority sweep, render search TPS + indexing TPS over time with search p99 overlaid and the SLO line, so the graph shows the breaking point rather than just a shape.

title: Confirm whether production stella applies the instruct prompt
description: stella400m defaults to PROMPT_MODE=always, which prepends the Stella instruct prompt server-side. Stella is asymmetric, so this changes the vector: query-side and passage-side embeddings are not comparable. If the employer service encodes without a prompt, this deployment is not reproducing production and the sweep numbers are for a slightly different workload. Needs a one-line answer from someone with access to the production encode path. If the answer is 'no prompt', flip PROMPT_MODE to never in config.pbtxt and re-run the sweep (triton-throughput-tester-6fx) so both changes land together.

title: Wire stella400m into a 400M-scale intent pipeline
description: stella400m is only the encoder half. To reproduce the production intent shape at 400M, add a second config entry pointing at the same checkpoint directory with PROMPT_MODE=never (corpus indexing must NOT get the instruct prompt -- Stella is asymmetric and prompting both sides collapses every similarity into 0.96-0.9999), then have the retrieval step score the corpus with the corpus-side model and the query with the query-side model. Open question still unanswered by the user: does production return the corpus string, the intent label, or both? Also decide whether configuration.py and modeling.py should be vendored into triton-models/stella400m/1/ so the deployment is rebuildable from the repo alone; they are currently remote-only.
close_reason: Premise was wrong. User confirmed production stella is a pure embedding service: it returns embeddings and does no cosine similarity and involves no corpus. There is no 400M intent pipeline to build on top of this model. Both open questions in the description are now resolved: (1) retrieval is out of scope for stella400m entirely, (2) configuration.py/modeling.py and the rest of the checkpoint metadata are now vendored into triton-models/stella400m/1/, so the deployment is rebuildable from the repo (only model.safetensors is downloaded).

title: Re-run stella sweep wired on the 1 Gb switch
description:
CORRECTED PREMISE: the wifi ssh link was never in the request path. sweep.sh and priorityload.py run the load generator INSIDE the container over localhost, so the ssh hop carries only the shell and the summary text. Re-running on the 1 Gb switch will NOT move the flat ic1 ~110 rps. That flatness is server-side: GPU pinned at ~35% sm with conc=64 matching conc=16 is serialisation inside one python-backend instance's execute(), which is why instance_group.count is the lever. See the 2026-11-05 correction entry in PROGRESS_LOG.md.

What is still worth doing, and why:
1. A client-side ramp-up.py run against stella IS network-bound (generator on the laptop), so it needs the wired link. Confirm the ic4 knee holds and whether ic6/ic8 continue the curve. Measure the noise floor properly.
2. Higher-value replacement: fix the generator so it can offer its target rate (see triton-throughput-tester follow-up in README), then re-run the co-tenancy ramp to pin down indexing headroom between 30 and 80 rps.

title: Sweep query length and corpus size on intent-replica
description: Batching and CPU-vs-GPU cosine are now measured (see git log 91dffa9): batching dominates, worth 5.3x over the production shape. Remaining axes: (1) query token length 10-25 - the encoder is now the ceiling at 52% GPU sm, so this is the highest-value remaining sweep; (2) corpus size - try build_corpus.py --limit 8000/16000 to see how rps scales, which isolates the bandwidth cost; (3) max_queue_delay_microseconds (currently 5000) - at conc=64 batches reached 28 rows, a longer delay may reach max_batch_size 128; (4) max_batch_size 128 vs 64. Use tools/measure.sh which reports req_per_exec and GPU sm together.

value: stella400m is a pure embedding service (text -> 1024-d unit-norm vector). Production does NOT do cosine similarity and has NO corpus. Do not add retrieval/corpus logic to triton-models/stella400m/ — that shape belongs to intent-replica, a separate model. The checkpoint code (modeling.py, configuration.py, config.json, tokenizer, pooling/head configs) is vendored in triton-models/stella400m/1/ and sha256-matched to the box; only model.safetensors (1.7 GB) is downloaded.

Triton model repo is bind-mounted host /AI/models/triton -> container /opt/ml/model, so model files are at /opt/ml/model/<model>/<version>/. Never sed a container path from the host: it fails silently and yields uniformly wrong measurements. Confirm the LOADED config with GET :8000/v2/models/<name>/config, not the file.

git push over HTTPS fails here (no credential helper). Push with: git push git@github.com:jdchmiel/triton-throughput-learning.git main. Do NOT run bd dolt push - this repo has no Dolt remote and needs none; the pre-commit hook exports beads into the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl, so git push is the only sync step. See AGENTS.md 'Beads Sync Model'.

nvidia-smi dmon -s um columns are: gpu sm mem enc dec jpg ofa fb bar1 ccpm (sm=$2, mem=$3, fb=$8), header is 2 lines. awk compares strings unless you write $2+0, which silently makes every max wrong. Real Triton batch size = delta nv_inference_request_success / delta nv_inference_exec_count, scoped to the gpu_uuid= variant of the metric.
